essence: Optics Compensation radially remaps the image around a chosen optical center, converting between a flat rectilinear view and a wide-angle/fisheye-like projection. Increasing Field Of View increases the strength of that projection remap; Reverse Lens Distortion switches to the inverse direction for lens-distortion correction, while Resize can enlarge the result to hide remap-created edge gaps.
manifests_as: Straight lines near the frame edges bend or unbend around the view center, often with stretched corners and transparent/cropped borders unless the result is resized.

key_levers.name: Field Of View (FOV)
key_levers.effect: This is the distortion amount: 0 leaves the image visually unchanged, while larger values apply progressively stronger radial wide-angle projection remapping.

key_levers.name: Reverse Lens Distortion
key_levers.effect: Switches the radial remap to its inverse direction, making the effect useful for undoing rather than adding the corresponding lens-distortion shape.

key_levers.name: FOV Orientation
key_levers.effect: Chooses which image dimension the FOV value is measured across, changing how the same numeric FOV maps to the frame aspect ratio.

key_levers.name: Optimal Pixels (Invalidates Reversal)
key_levers.effect: Enables the effect's Optimal Pixels mode; this mode invalidates/overrides Reverse Lens Distortion, so it cannot be used as an inverse-distortion correction switch at the same time.

key_levers.name: Resize
key_levers.effect: Controls post-remap enlargement to trade away more of the source image in exchange for fewer empty or transparent borders created by the distortion.

reasoning_hooks: The default FOV is 0, so the effect can be present yet produce no visible geometric change.
Reverse Lens Distortion is direction control, not additional intensity; set FOV first, then choose the direction that bends lines toward the desired correction.
Optimal Pixels (Invalidates Reversal)=1 disables the usefulness of Reverse Lens Distortion; turn Optimal Pixels off when evaluating normal versus inverse correction.
View Center is the radial pivot: an off-center lens distortion must be centered on the real optical axis, or correction will improve one side while worsening the other.
Resize only manages edge coverage after the remap; it does not replace choosing an appropriate FOV or correction direction.
Large FOV changes are most legible on footage with straight architectural lines near the edges; low-detail or center-only imagery may make tuning direction ambiguous.
